title: The Possible, the Plausible, and the Desirable: Event-Based Modality Detection for Language Processing
research_question: Can modality be modeled and automatically detected at the event level by identifying open-class modal triggers, assigning them a linguistically grounded fine-grained sense, and linking each trigger to the event it modifies?
methodology: The authors transform the Georgetown Gradable Modal Expressions corpus, derived from MPQA and containing about 11,000 sentences, into an event-based modality dataset with modal triggers, modal senses, and modified-event information, using spaCy analyses and the head of each annotated proposition as the event head. They reserve 10% of the shuffled data for testing and use five train-validation folds on the remainder. Experiments cover oracle-trigger modal-sense classification, joint trigger detection and sense classification, and detection of modalized event spans or heads. Majority-vote baselines are compared with RoBERTa-base sequence models, with BIOSE-style tagging, CRF decoding for longer spans, and precision, recall, and F1 reported using CoNLL evaluation.

key_findings.finding: Restricting modality to a small closed set of modal auxiliary verbs makes detection much easier than allowing modal triggers from arbitrary syntactic classes; for example, RoBERTa modal-versus-nonmodal F1 drops from 99.9 on the six modal verbs to 73.2 on all trigger types.

When a modal trigger is already known, contextual information improves sense classification, especially for fine-grained senses: the full-context RoBERTa condition reaches 76.4 F1 versus 72.0 for majority voting, while masking the trigger reduces F1 to 58.3.
For unrestricted trigger detection and classification, RoBERTa consistently improves over the majority-vote baseline; fine-grained labeled F1 is 58.14 compared with 51.29 for the baseline.
Gold event-head information substantially helps modal-trigger tagging, but using predicted event heads can reduce performance because event-prediction errors propagate into trigger classification.

Modal-trigger information improves detection of the event being modified: modal/nonmodal event-span F1 rises from 51.1 without trigger information to 71.13 with a gold trigger, although predicted-trigger information gives only 53.55.
key_findings.section: 5. Results — Event Detection Based on Modal Triggers

key_findings.finding: The proposed taxonomy separates priority-related modality into rules and norms, desires and wishes, and plans and goals, while plausibility is divided according to knowledge, state of the world, and state of the agent.
key_findings.section: 3. Event-Based Modality Detection: Proposed Task Definition

key_findings.finding: Manual inspection of development-set errors found that a substantial fraction of apparent model errors were actually missed or incorrect gold annotations, indicating incomplete coverage in the underlying annotation.

limitations: The GME corpus annotates MPQA material rather than workplace e-mail or chat, so the reported performance does not directly establish effectiveness on organizational communication.
Modality is related to but distinct from speech acts: the task does not directly classify utterances as requests, commitments, decisions, promises, assignments, or responses.
The representation links modal triggers to events but does not extract action owners, recipients, detailed action objects, deadlines, temporal constraints, or execution conditions.
Fine-grained unrestricted trigger classification remains difficult, with substantially lower F1 than detection restricted to a closed list of modal auxiliary verbs.
Gold event-head information is highly beneficial whereas predicted event heads can hurt performance, showing substantial sensitivity to upstream prediction errors.

The oracle-trigger sense-classification experiments have 73%-79% trigger-lemma overlap between training and development/test data, and the authors note that this partly explains the strong majority-vote baseline.
The authors' manual error analysis indicates that the gold corpus has incomplete modal-trigger coverage, so measured precision and recall are affected by annotation errors.
For some fine-grained experimental reporting, wishes and goals are merged into an 'intentions' category because of data sparsity, reducing fidelity to the full proposed taxonomy.
The experiments use shuffled corpus splits rather than an explicit cross-domain or workplace-domain evaluation, leaving robustness to new genres unresolved.
raw_claims: The paper defines event-based modality detection as finding modal triggers, their senses, and the events they modify.
Modal triggers are allowed to come from any part of speech rather than only from a predefined list of auxiliary verbs.
The modal taxonomy has two broad branches, Priority and Plausibility, each divided into three finer-grained senses.
The processed GME data includes sentences without modality rather than restricting evaluation to sentences known to contain modal triggers.
The authors evaluate modal-sense classification, trigger detection with sense classification, and detection of modalized events.
RoBERTa-base is fine-tuned as the principal contextual sequence model and compared with majority-vote baselines.
Detection performance drops markedly when moving from six conventional modal verbs to unrestricted modal expressions.
Full sentential context contributes to modal-sense disambiguation, while removing the trigger lemma substantially harms performance.
RoBERTa improves over the majority-vote baseline for unrestricted trigger detection at both coarse and fine sense granularities.
Gold event-head information improves trigger tagging, whereas predicted heads introduce error propagation.
Providing modal-trigger information improves identification of the associated event span compared with detecting modal events without trigger information.
Manual review of model errors indicates that some apparent false positives and false negatives are errors or omissions in the gold annotation.
The authors release code, trained-model-related experimental resources, evaluation scripts, and a processed version of the modality corpus.
